WORLDS ARE PRODUCTION-PRODUCED. Happy arms drive the SHIPPED journey (openStore + driveThrough(store,"goal.close")). The store is APPEND-ONLY, so a committed event cannot be byte-edited in place: every refusal world is a REPLICA — drive the journey, read its three durable payloads (GoalExecutionEnabled on goal-1, BodiesSealed + EnvelopeSealed on planning-authority/run-1), re-commit those exact bytes into a fresh store with ONE field mutated. The replica commits the ENVELOPE event FIRST so a take-first (index) selection in the reader is observable. Its own POSITIVE CONTROL is asserted before any refusal arm ("accepts an UNMUTATED replica"), so a replica whose bytes never reached the reader cannot make every negative arm pass for the wrong reason.

POSITIVE ARMS (4): revision byte-identical to decoding the store's OWN BodiesSealed bytes independently (anti-tautology — operand is the store, not a literal) + planHash/revisionId/graphRevisionRef/runId/authorityRef; steps[{description,stepId,kind}] exposed (c320c34a's row needs statements, not hashes); witness.bodiesDigest === payload.bodiesDigest; criteria arm with obligations[].statement + criteriaDigest/criteriaRef.

REFUSAL ARMS: 18-entry table driven by it.each, each pinning [code, layer] EXACTLY, `detail` where two worlds share a code, and `source` = [code, layer] of the layer that actually answered. Every arm additionally asserts the refusal carries NO revision/contract/planHash/revisionId/criteriaDigest/runId (UNKNOWN never becomes empty). Codes: APPROVAL_ABSENT (x2: never-activated / SUPERSEDED validity), APPROVAL_AMBIGUOUS (two GoalExecutionEnabled — store-level because the goal reducer refuses a second activate), APPROVAL_MALFORMED (x2: unparseable payload / PARTIALLY bound witness, which must NOT read as legacy), LEGACY_UNBOUND (four keys ABSENT), LOCATOR_MISMATCH (authorityRef names another aggregate — locator is not evidence), SEAL_ABSENT (x2 bodies/envelope), SEAL_AMBIGUOUS, SEAL_MALFORMED, PROJECT_MISMATCH, WITNESS_DIGEST_MISMATCH (x2 bodies/envelope digest swapped under the witness), BODIES_INVALID with source PLAN_REVISION_DIGEST_MISMATCH@PLAN_REVISION_DIGEST (one authorRef char tampered — same length so the CANONICALIZATION layer cannot be what answers), SEAL_DIGEST_MISMATCH (a VALID re-minted revision substituted: both codecs green, both digest fields agree, only the framed recompute notices), ENVELOPE_INVALID with source PLANNING_AUTHORITY_REVISION_MISMATCH@PLANNING_AUTHORITY_ENVELOPE, ENVELOPE_DIVERGED (FULL splice: a valid envelope re-encoded for run-other with bindings.runId AND submission.runId moved together so the codec's RUN_MISMATCH stays satisfied, its digest restated on payload AND witness — only a cross-EVENT comparison can refuse).

DECISIONS WORTH THE RECORD:
1. CANONICALITY IS DELEGATED. decodePlanRevisionBytes/decodeAcceptanceContractBytes/decodePlanningAuthorityEnvelopeBytes each already re-encode and byte-compare their admitted content and verify the carried digest; a second opinion here would be a fork, so their code+layer travel out verbatim under `source` and are never restamped.

Step 1 measured `bodiesDigestOf` private at planning-authority-persistence.ts:104; this row adds ONLY the `export` keyword to that one declaration (the declared one-line producer edit) so the reader recomputes with the WRITER's own function. comments.content:
PREREQUISITE LANDED — the goal→run→bodies join your readers need now exists end-to-end. task-2cc6c59d committed at ada30c1 (worker-40cfc767), on top of task-074e6d2e at 132d506 which made the shipped journey seal anything at all.

WHAT YOU CAN NOW READ, field by field. The durable `GoalExecutionEnabled` event on the GOAL aggregate carries `payload.activation` with SEVEN keys — the core's original three plus four bound by this row:
    activeGraphRevisionRef, graphApprovalRef, truthClass      (unchanged, core's)
    runId                                                     (the approved run)
    authorityRef        = planningAuthorityAggregateId(runId) = "planning-authority/<runId>"
    envelopeDigest      (copied from the run's durable record)
    bodiesDigest        (copied from the PlanningAuthorityBodiesSealed payload)
So the join is: goal aggregate -> that one event -> `activation.runId` -> `planning-authority/<runId>` -> the sealed bodies. No caller field is bound anywhere in that chain; every value is read back out of a durable record written by a production writer.

THREE THINGS THAT WILL COST YOU TIME IF YOU LEARN THEM THE HARD WAY:
1. `bodiesDigest` is TWO-SOURCE and that is permanent, not an oversight. `commitFinalizedSubmission` freezes the run record's binding to `{authorityRef, envelopeDigest}` EXACTLY, so the digest is NOT on the run record even on the happy path. Its only durable home is the `PlanningAuthorityBodiesSealed` payload. Widening the record's binding means editing `planning-authority-finalize.ts`, which taskRail forbids on this lineage.
2. `readDurableLedger` CANNOT see the authority aggregate. It folds only `decision.targetAggregateId`, and the authority leg is SECONDARY, so a ledger read reports it empty forever regardless of what was sealed. Use `store.readEvents(planningAuthorityAggregateId(runId))`.
3. SELECT AUTHORITY EVENTS BY TYPE, NEVER BY INDEX. `PlanningAuthorityBodiesSealed` and `PlanningAuthorityEnvelopeSealed` land on that same aggregate and their write order is UNPINNED. A take-first read (the `persistence.test.ts:134` shape) names whichever landed first and stays green while reading the wrong payload. Related hazard, reported to the seam owner and not fixed by either row: the bodies type literal exists as SIX unexported, differently-named private constants — a rename at the writer silently nulls every string-matched read and presents as "no authority carried".

THREE NEW REFUSALS your readers may meet, each with its own stable code at layer `APPROVAL_RUN_BINDING`: `APPROVAL_RUN_NOT_REVIEWABLE` (run not at lifecycle PLAN_REVIEW), `APPROVAL_GRAPH_REVISION_DIVERGED` (caller's graphRevisionRef ≠ the RUN RECORD's), `APPROVAL_AUTHORITY_UNSEALED` (any of authorityRef / envelopeDigest / bodiesDigest unreadable — all three or nothing, never a partial bind). An unknown run and a hash mismatch still answer BOOTSTRAP_PREREQUISITE_MISSING and BOOTSTRAP_REVISION_HASH_MISMATCH at DAEMON_PREREQUISITE, unrestamped.

ONE PLANNING NOTE THAT MAY SIMPLIFY YOUR ROW: the caller-vs-sealed graphRevisionRef question is already closed on the write side. `planning-authority-envelope.ts:99-101` refuses PLANNING_AUTHORITY_GRAPH_REVISION_MISMATCH when the sealed plan body's graph revision disagrees with the submission's, so on any SEALED run the run record's copy and the authority payload's copy are equal by construction. If your plan carries a "which graphRevisionRef" disambiguation step, it can cite that guard instead of re-deriving it — I measured it by trying to build the divergent world and being refused.
